note: CAC-GP-1.8. The source of truth for what is a guard. Discovery used to glob four filename patterns, which let eight real guards escape — seven copies of decisions-render.sh plus ai-register/exposure.sh, none of them ever mutation-tested, and the GP-1.7 registry check filtered through the same list so it confirmed its own blind spot (BL-101). Filename convention could never have caught both: seven shared a name no convention anticipated, and the eighth shared nothing with anything. This file classifies EVERY skills/*/evals/*.sh. A script in none of these lists fails the run — that is the whole point, and it is why the registry lists non-guards too.

roles.guard: Proved under CAC-GP-1. Must have skills/<skill>/evals/guard-proofs/<name>.json with one mutation per half.
roles.candidate: Guard-shaped by the standard's own definition, not yet enrolled because it has no registered mutation. Counted and printed on every run so the number is visible rather than implied. Enrolment is BL-99.
roles.not-a-guard: Asserts what the product DOES, or checks the environment. Not a defect-cannot-occur property.
